blogs.title: Beyond Type 1 and 2: Unmasking HNF1A-MODY in the Young Adult
blogs.description: This post explores the diagnostic dilemma of young-onset diabetes, focusing on why traditional markers like BMI and autoantibodies can be misleading. We analyze the specific clinical clues in this case—including the profound family history across three generations, the discrepancy between severe hyperglycemia and preserved C-peptide, and the unique finding of glycosuria without DKA—to build a framework for when to suspect Monogenic Diabetes over classic Type 1 or Type 2.

blogs.title: The Therapeutic Pivot: Why Sulfonylureas (or GLP-1s) Beat Insulin in HNF1A-MODY
blogs.description: Focusing on management tension, this article discusses the 'de-insulinization' strategy once HNF1A-MODY is confirmed. We examine the pathophysiology of the defective KATP channel in beta cells that makes these patients exquisitely sensitive to sulfonylureas, while also reviewing emerging data supporting GLP-1 receptor agonists as a modern alternative to avoid hypoglycemia. The post details how switching from a complex insulin/metformin/saxagliptin regimen to targeted oral/GLP-1 therapy rapidly normalized this patient's HbA1c from 10.2% to 6.0%.

blogs.title: Novel Variants and Precision Medicine: Interpreting a 'New' Mutation in HNF1A
blogs.description: This post addresses the challenges of Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS) reporting when a patient carries a variant not yet listed in major databases like ClinVar. Using the case's discovery of p.N270S, we walk through the ACMG guidelines for classifying Variants of Uncertain Significance (VUS) versus Likely Pathogenic variants based on segregation data, AlphaMissense scores, and functional domains. It serves as a guide for clinicians on how to trust genetic results even when they represent novel discoveries.

blogs.title: Autonomic Neuropathy and Renal Thresholds: Hidden Clues in HNF1A-MODY
blogs.description: While often overlooked, extra-pancreatic manifestations can provide critical diagnostic hints for HNF1A mutations. This blog delves into the case's finding of severely reduced sudomotor function (autonomic neuropathy) and explains the mechanism behind glycosuria caused by downregulated SGLT2 expression in renal tubules due to HNF1A deficiency. We discuss why recognizing these specific phenotypes can expedite genetic testing before full-blown complications arise.

blogs.title: The Pitfalls of Standardized Tools: Applying MODY Probability Calculators in Diverse Populations
blogs.description: Critiquing current diagnostic algorithms, this post analyzes the limitations of tools like the Exeter MODY Calculator when applied to non-European populations. By examining how this Asian patient scored only a 62% probability despite clear clinical evidence, we discuss how rising global obesity rates blur the distinction between MODY and Type 2 diabetes, arguing that reliance solely on calculators may miss significant numbers of monogenic cases that require genetic confirmation.
